H72.statement: Use orbit-specific transition congruences beyond distinctness modulo six to strengthen P72 enough to exclude every infinite coefficient-safe tail.

NG21.abstract_countermodel: enumerate the positive integers coprime to six and set Y_(i+1)=Y_i*(1+1/(3*x_i))
NG21.hypothesis: Distinctness, a fixed lower bound, and gcd(x_i,6)=1 alone imply Y_j=O(j^gamma) for some gamma<1/9.
NG21.scope: This refutes only an improvement using the packing premises alone; actual Collatz transition congruences may still yield a stronger exponent.
NG21.sharpness_proof: two admissible integers per six-number block give sum 1/x_i=(1/3)log(j)+O(1); log(1+1/(3x))=1/(3x)+O(1/x^2), hence log(Y_j)=log(j)/9+O(1)

what_this_result_does_not_prove: Sharpness of the coarse packing input is not an example of a Collatz orbit and does not show that exponent 1/9 is dynamically optimal.
